Norman uses the named secondary scPerturb release from Zenodo record 7278143 version 1.1 \citep{scperturb2024state}. Its documented transformation reads the original count matrix without expression normalization. We retain source-annotated good-coverage singlet assignments and explicitly negative-control constructs, preserve guide provenance, and match by gemgroup. This is distinct from a GEARS compatibility track. The initial library range is 500--20,000 counts, with at least 50 cells per condition. After source-specific exclusions and target-pair aggregation, the prepared dataset has 105 singles, 126 pairs, and 10,623 eligible genes; 88 pairs are development conditions and 38 are final test conditions.

Gene eligibility uses controls and singles only. A gene survives if at least one reference condition has normalized mean at least 0.1 and detection fraction at least 0.01. This frozen universe is the primary output; it does not establish performance on genes excluded by the reference rule. Source hashes, count locations, guide mapping, exclusions, normalization parameters, gene order, and split manifests are retained. Held-out pair responses occupy a separate evaluator bundle and are unavailable to model fitting or architecture selection.

Random pair holdout reserves 30\% of canonical unordered pairs, using identities alone. Five development folds determine candidate errors and stopping epochs. The initial CPU search uses ranks 2 and 8, ridge penalties 1 and 100, and at most 80 epochs for neural candidates. AdamW uses learning rate 0.01 and weight decay 0.01, with full-batch equal-condition loss. Initial screening uses one optimization seed; real-data finalist evaluation uses five seeds, while synthetic engineering finalists use two. Final neural predictions average five refitted seeds. The selected neural family and the selected simpler comparator are chosen separately on development error and fixed before final evaluation. Their comparison can therefore reject the neural structural claim even when the network beats additivity.

Metric controls include a zero effect, observed additivity, development mean residual, an oracle response as an explicit positive control, and 100 pair permutations of evaluator residuals. These are diagnostics rather than newly eligible candidates. On Wessels, permuted residuals retain mean response Pearson correlation 0.5638 and residual cosine 0.2516 despite MSE 0.020850, above additive MSE 0.013937. The zero-effect prediction also has positive residual cosine 0.6990 while its additive skill is negative. Positive alignment alone can therefore be driven by shared reference geometry and cannot establish useful prediction.

On each genetic development set, three seeds define five outer random folds and five outer partner folds, with three inner folds of the corresponding protocol per outer fit. An expanded linear comparator selects among 25 configurations comprising a shared offset and global, ridge, and rank-four reduced-rank models at eight penalties. The kernel procedure reduces outer-validation MSE relative to this comparator by 1.78--2.70\% for Norman random holdouts, 1.13--3.38\% for Norman partner holdouts, 2.50--3.98\% for Wessels random holdouts, and 0.83--1.00\% for Wessels partner holdouts. These are development-only point estimates across dependent resamplings, not independent confirmation. The search spaces and budgets differ, so these results do not establish a capacity-matched structural advantage.

The kernel procedure reduces outer-validation MSE relative to this comparator by 1.78--2.70\% for Norman random holdouts, 1.13--3.38\% for Norman partner holdouts, 2.50--3.98\% for Wessels random holdouts, and 0.83--1.00\% for Wessels partner holdouts. These are development-only point estimates across dependent resamplings, not independent confirmation. The search spaces and budgets differ, so these results do not establish a capacity-matched structural advantage.

GenePT, ESM2, GO and Hallmark kernels are also tested against an identically searched shuffled-gene-identity bank. Norman random folds and both expanded random tracks retain the measured-only baseline. Original Wessels random-fold MSE improves from 0.00503184 to 0.00500368 with real priors, but shuffling also improves it to 0.00501316. Norman partner error worsens slightly with real priors. Small improvements on the expanded partner tracks do not establish a general identity-specific benefit.

We therefore separately download the scPerturb release of the Replogle K562 essential-gene CRISPRi screen \citep{replogle2022} and verify its publisher MD5. It contains 310,385 cells, 8,563 output genes and 2,057 single-target conditions. Of these, 2,002 targets map to the supplied GO dictionary. A seed-fixed 1,601/401 training/validation target split trains a 16-to-32-to-16 encoder for 200 updates against training-target response PCs. Its normalized validation-PC MSE is 0.87670, versus 0.88021 for an alpha-ten ridge and 0.90792 for the training mean. These are source-task development scores.

Later source-selected family scores do not replace the unfavorable frozen result.

Source-context selection chooses width 128, latent dimension 32 and 120 epochs; final checkpoint selection uses only allowed reference rows. Its chemical pilot MSE is 8.8\% below the selected kernel. Positive-cosine nearest-three graphs derive only from allowed single profiles instead of external ontology graphs; observations are aggregate means. Five partner folds overlap; their per-occurrence mean differs from scoring averaged repeated predictions.

This pilot does not establish a material contribution that would justify adding a learned representation.
